read_by_is_every_reader_not_every_mentio: Widened from six entries to ten on 2026-08-14. The key claims to be every program and document that reads this file, and it was not: DEVPOST.md, JUDGING-AXES.md, VIDEO-KIT.md and PUBLIC-FLIP-CHECKLIST.md each tell a reader to take demo_url or video_url from here rather than from their own prose, which is reading. Paths that merely NAME this file in a sentence - README.md, docs/CI-STATE.md, docs/TOOL-USAGE.md, docs/deploy/JUDGE-PACK.md, docs/deploy/OBSERVABILITY.md, scripts/deploy/demo_acceptance.py, scripts/deploy/local_furl.py and others - are deliberately not listed, because a list that counted mentions would stop being the list of things that break when a value here changes.
never_write_a_credential_here: This file becomes world-readable the moment the repository is flipped public. judge_access.credentials_location is a POINTER to where a credential lives, never the credential itself. scripts/submission/check_submission_ready.py scans every value in this file and refuses if any of them is credential-shaped.
a_field_is_resolved_only_when_it_is_prov: Two fields below hold the sentinel because the fact they would assert is not true yet, not because nobody got round to typing them. Writing a value here that the world does not carry is the one failure this file exists to prevent: the gate would go green and a judge would still meet a 404.

judge_access.how: A judge reads the live CockroachDB Cloud ledger by either of two published paths: point any MCP client at the CockroachDB Managed MCP Server with the configuration in verticals/mainline/demo/judge/MCP-CONFIG.md section 1, or connect psql to the read-only mainline_judge SQL login in docs/deploy/JUDGE-PACK.md, which read all 14 mainline_audit views and was refused on all 11 base tables and write attempts when it was measured (evidence/deploy/judge-access.json).
judge_access.credentials_location: The submission form's judge-credentials field carries the mainline_judge password. It is generated by `python scripts/deploy/judge_access.py provision --rotate --show-password`, printed once to that run's terminal, and written to no file in this repository, no evidence artefact and no environment variable. This key is a pointer; it must never hold the value it points at.

notes.repo_url: RESOLVED, and the repository behind it is PUBLIC. Measured on 2026-08-12: `gh repo view Shaugato/mainline --json visibility,licenseInfo` answered {"visibility":"PUBLIC","licenseInfo":{"key":"apache-2.0"}}, and `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/master...HEAD` answered 0 0, so the tree a stranger clones is the tree that was audited. This note used to say the URL answered 404 to everyone but the owner; that sentence described a private repository and stopped being true when the flip landed. Resolving the string and flipping visibility remain two different facts and check_submission_ready.py still reports them as two, because they can diverge again: repo_url is a value in this file, visibility is asked of GitHub live on every run and is never read from a cached artefact. A judge needs no credential of ours to read any of it.
notes.demo_url: Unresolved because `terraform apply` has not been run: no MAINLINE Lambda, no Function URL, no bucket exists in the account. The plan that would create it is committed at evidence/deploy/terraform-plan-furl.txt and reads, at line 843, `Plan: 24 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.` - 11 resources in module.api[0] and 13 in module.guard[0], the cost guard infra/envs/demo/main.tf:631 instantiates, with authorization_type NONE at line 351, in ap-southeast-1. This note said `11 to add` until 2026-08-14; the 11 is the API module alone and stopped being the plan's total when the guard was wired in. The artefact is authoritative and this note is derived: the note was re-read against the plan, and the plan was not edited to agree with the note. The command is `MAINLINE_APPLY_APPROVED=1 scripts/deploy/deploy.sh --expect-account <id>`, and the hostname it prints is the value that belongs here. Two things must both be true before this field is written, and they fail independently: the ORIGIN must exist, and the app behind it must ANSWER. Rule 2 asks for a URL to a *functional* demo, so the second is checked by evidence/deploy/acceptance.json and by `python scripts/submission/check_submission_ready.py --check-urls`, which fetches the URL and requires HTTP 200 rather than trusting that it was pasted correctly. Writing a hostname here before both hold would turn this gate green and still hand a judge a broken page, which is the single failure this file exists to prevent.
